reply_text:
I wouldn't merge this yet. The extension parsing doesn't match what the README says, so in practice almost no upload gets the right content type. I made no changes. I read the diff and ran the new functions on a few sample filenames.

**Blocker: `extensionOf` (src/extension.js)**
`name.split('.')[1]` takes the text after the **first** dot and never lowercases it. The README says it should be the text after the **last** dot, lowercased. Actual results:

| filename | extension returned | expected | content type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Archive.TAR.GZ` | `"TAR"` | `gz` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `photo.JPG` | `"JPG"` | `jpg` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `my.photo.png` | `"photo"` | `png` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `README` | `undefined` | `""` | octet-stream |
| `file.` | `""` | `""` | ✓ |

So uppercase extensions and any name with more than one dot (including `.tar.gz`) silently fall back to `application/octet-stream`. A name with no dot also returns `undefined` instead of the documented empty string. Something like this would fix it:
```js
const i = name.lastIndexOf('.');
return i === -1 ? '' : name.slice(i + 1).toLowerCase();
```
It's your call whether a dotfile like `.env` should have extension `env`. The README doesn't say.

**Tests**
The only extension test is `photo.jpg`, which passes only because it's lowercase with a single dot. Before merging, add tests for the README's own examples (`Archive.TAR.GZ`, `photo.JPG`), plus a name with no dot and one with a trailing dot. There are no tests for `contentType` at all.

**`safeName`: fine for path traversal, one gap**
- Slashes and backslashes become `_` and leading dots are removed, so it can't climb a directory: `../../x` → `x`, `a/../b` → `a_.._b`.
- The gap: `..` or `...` become an **empty string**. If anything uses that as a stored filename, it could end up writing to the upload directory itself. It should reject empty results or fall back to a default name.
- Removing the leading dot also changes a dotfile's name (`.env` → `env`). That's probably fine, but worth knowing.

**Minor**
- `TYPES` has only four entries. Fine for a first version, but common ones like `jpeg`, `gif`, `txt` and `zip` will come through as octet-stream.
- The CHANGELOG entry doesn't mention `safeName`.

The version bump to 0.5.0 and the README additions look fine.
